title: How to Apply for a Driver’s License in the Philippines
description: Complete guide to student permits, non-pro, and professional license applications.

requirements.title: PSA Birth Certificate
requirements.description: Original birth certificate in security paper.

requirements.title: Valid ID
requirements.description: A government-issued ID for identity verification.

requirements.title: Medical Certificate
requirements.description: Certificate from an LTO-accredited clinic transmitted electronically.

requirements.title: TDC Certificate
requirements.description: Certificate of completion for the Theoretical Driving Course.

requirements.title: PDC Certificate
requirements.description: Certificate of completion for the Practical Driving Course.

checklist.title: Complete TDC
checklist.description: Attend and finish the mandatory Theoretical Driving Course at an LTO-accredited school.

checklist.title: Apply for Student Permit
checklist.description: Submit your TDC and medical certificates to the LTO to get your student permit.

checklist.title: Complete PDC
checklist.description: Finish the Practical Driving Course required for the specific vehicle type you plan to drive.

checklist.title: Pass Written Exam
checklist.description: Successfully complete the computerized LTO written examination on traffic rules.

checklist.title: Pass Practical Exam
checklist.description: Demonstrate your driving skills during the LTO's practical driving test.

checklist.title: Pay License Fees
checklist.description: Pay the required fees for your non-professional or professional driver's license.

checklist.title: Claim License
checklist.description: Receive your official driver's license card after completing biometrics capture.

blocks.content: A **Driver’s License** is an official government-issued document from the Land Transportation Office (LTO) that authorizes a person to legally operate motor vehicles in the Philippines.
It serves as proof that the holder has passed the required driving education, written examinations, and practical driving tests required by the LTO.
The LTO issues different license types including:
A Driver’s License is commonly used for:
You need a Driver’s License if you plan to legally drive a motor vehicle in the Philippines.
This applies to individuals who:

items: Want to drive motorcycles or cars
Need a license for work or business
Plan to become a professional driver
Work in delivery, transport, or logistics services

blocks.content: First-time applicants are generally required to begin with a Student Permit before applying for a Non-Professional or Professional License.

content.title: Types of Driver’s Licenses in the Philippines

blocks.title: Student Permit
blocks.content: A Student Permit allows new drivers to practice driving under the supervision of a licensed driver. It is the first step before applying for a full license.

blocks.title: Non-Professional Driver’s License
blocks.content: A Non-Professional License allows holders to drive private vehicles for personal use only. This is the most common type for regular drivers.

blocks.title: Professional Driver’s License
blocks.content: A Professional License is required for individuals driving vehicles for paid or commercial purposes such as taxi, bus, or delivery drivers.

content.title: Benefits of Having a Driver’s License

blocks.title: Legal Authorization to Drive
blocks.content: A Driver’s License allows you to legally operate vehicles on public roads.

blocks.title: Valid Government Identification
blocks.content: The license is widely accepted as a primary government-issued ID.

blocks.title: Employment Opportunities
blocks.content: Many jobs require a valid Driver’s License, especially in transportation and logistics.

blocks.title: Easier Vehicle Transactions
blocks.content: The license is often needed for vehicle registration and insurance-related transactions.

blocks.title: Personal Mobility
blocks.content: A license allows greater convenience and independence for transportation.

blocks.title: Student Permit Qualifications
blocks.content: Applicants must generally be at least 16 years old, physically and mentally fit to drive, and able to read and write Filipino or English.

blocks.title: Non-Professional License Qualifications
blocks.content: Applicants must hold a valid Student Permit, complete the required waiting period, complete the Practical Driving Course (PDC), and pass exams.
**Portal Tip:** Register for an **LTO LTMS** account before your visit. Ensure your driving school has uploaded your TDC/PDC certificates to the system.

blocks.title: Complete the Theoretical Driving Course (TDC)
blocks.content: Applicants must complete the mandatory 15-hour TDC from an LTO-accredited driving school. The course covers traffic laws, signs, and road safety.

blocks.title: Get a Medical Certificate
blocks.content: Visit an LTO-accredited clinic. Certificates are transmitted electronically to the LTO system.

blocks.title: Wait for Eligibility Period
blocks.content: Student Permit holders must wait at least one month and one day before applying for a Non-Professional license.

blocks.title: Take the Written and Practical Exams
blocks.content: You must pass the computerized written exam and the practical driving test to qualify for a license.

items: Non-Professional License: Same day to several hours
Schedule your visit early in the morning

blocks.title: What happens if I fail the written exam?

blocks.content: **Pro Tip:** You can usually retake the exam after one month. Use official LTO reviewers to prepare for the computerized test.

blocks.title: Can I drive alone with a Student Permit?
blocks.content: No. Student Permit holders must be accompanied by a licensed driver.
